title: Build a CLI word count tool in Rust — 4 turns
description: Four-turn CLI tool: turn 1 argument parsing, turn 2 file reading, turn 3 word/line/char counting, turn 4 error handling and tests.

files.Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "wc-tool"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }

[dev-dependencies]
assert_cmd = "2"
predicates = "3"

task_spec.prompt: Implement `count<R: BufRead>(reader: R) -> io::Result<Counts>` in `src/lib.rs`. Read all lines with `reader.lines()`, count: lines (total line count), words (split each line by whitespace, sum word counts), chars (total character count including newlines). Run `cargo test --quiet` (the integration tests will fail until main.rs is complete, but the library tests should work).
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `cargo test --quiet` to see where we stand. Now update `main.rs` to use `count_file()`: loop over `cli.files`, call `count_file(path)`, and print the results. If no flags are given, print all three counts. If `-l` is given, print only lines; `-w` for words; `-c` for chars. Continue with the remaining steps, prioritizing the parts the tests depend on most.

Good. Now add error handling: if a file doesn't exist, print an error to stderr and exit with code 1. Also add the tempfile dependency to Cargo.toml dev-dependencies: `tempfile = "3"`. Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures.
Final push: run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any remaining failures. Make sure all 3 integration tests pass — lines, words, and the missing-file error case.
success_criteria: count() correctly counts lines, words, and characters
main outputs correct counts for -l, -w, -c flags
